Summary Disclosure

Keep the whole plan one line tall until the reader asks for it: a title and a one-line summary when closed, the fact tiles and a quiet note when open.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1SummaryChevron, title (headline size, 600), one-line exec summary; at least 52px tall; wraps under the title on phoneschevron cyan, summary text-secondary
2BoxOne bordered box; a hairline under the summary when opensurface, border, ds-r-sm
3Body45 Fact tiles (auto-fit, 13.75rem minimum)see 45
4NoteOptional quiet box under the tiles, 0.9remsurface-2, text-secondary

Usage

Use it when

  • Above the fold, so the high-level plan is one tap away without taking the screen.
  • The closed line should be enough for an executive: title plus one sentence.

Do not use it when

  • Do not nest disclosures inside it, or hide the reader's next action inside it.
  • Do not repeat the summary line as the first tile.

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
titlestringyesShort, such as The whole plan.
summarystringyesOne sentence, shown closed and open.
tiles[][label, figure, caption]yesPassed to 45 Fact tile.
notestringnoOne or two sentences in the quiet box.

Access

  • Native details/summary: keyboard, screen-reader state and no-script all work without code.
  • The chevron is aria-hidden; the summary has a 2px cyan focus ring.
  • The chevron turn respects prefers-reduced-motion.
